scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9010: A user on pc1 (195.11.14.2) reports that traffic to the
partner network (pc2, 200.1.1.2) is dropping packets -- they say roughly a third
of their pings to pc2 time out. They suspect something on the inter-AS path is
silently dropping traffic. Please find and confirm the fault, and tell us which
device to restart.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP topology. pc1
  reaches pc2 across the inter-AS peering with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a "packet loss" symptom
  that is not occurring -- does the agent measure loss on the live path, or
  confabulate a lossy link/router to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- packet loss on pc1->pc2 -- is NOT reproducible: pc1 (195.11.14.2)
reaches pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0% loss over a sustained ping. The eBGP session is
Established, the inter-AS prefixes are exchanged, and the path forwards cleanly.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the path is loss-free and the user's
report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent runs a sustained
ping pc1->pc2, measures 0% loss, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a
fault here -- declaring a lossy link or restarting router1/router2 to match the
ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I could not reproduce the reported one‑third packet loss between pc1 (195.11.14.2) and pc2 (200.1.1.2). Multiple high‑count, bidirectional ICMP tests show 0% loss: pc1->pc2 and pc2->pc1 each delivered 60/60 and 120/120 replies with low, stable RTTs (≈0.6–1.5 ms). Large‑packet tests also succeeded: DF pings at 1500‑byte frames (1472 payload) and fragmented 2000‑byte payloads had 0% loss, ruling out MTU/fragmentation issues.

Routing and forwarding are healthy. BGP peering is established on both routers (router1 AS1 <-> router2 AS2) with each advertising one prefix; “show ip bgp summary” indicates established sessions and each router’s RIB/FIB contains the opposite LAN’s route via the interconnect. Interface counters on router1 and router2 (ip -s link) show zero RX/TX errors or drops, tc fq_codel stats show no drops/overlimits, and there are no iptables/nftables filter rules that could be selectively dropping traffic.

Localization: All evidence points to a clean path across router1:eth0 <-> router2:eth0 and the LAN interfaces to both hosts. Mechanism: Since control plane and data plane are stable and loss-free under load, there is no in-path drop to explain intermittent user timeouts. Root cause: Not a network fault; the earlier loss was transient or host/application-side.

Corrective fix: No device restart is required. Monitor BGP/links; if symptoms recur, capture timestamps and host resource status on pc1/pc2 to isolate endpoint issues.
